newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arafat accuses Israel of intransigence, delay.
newsitem.headline: Arafat accuses Israel of intransigence, delay.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, in a message to a U.N. body, accused the Israeli government on Friday of "intransigence, procrastination and circumvention."

He called on the international community to induce Israel to comply with agreements already signed. The object was to enable the Palestinian people to exercise their right of self-determination and to "establish an independent state with its capital at Jerusalem."

Arafat's message was read by the Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, at a meeting of the U.N. committee on the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people to mark the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People.

The day is observed annually on Nov. 29, corresponding to the date in 1947 when the U.N. General Assembly voted to partition Palestine into Arab and Jewish states, which Arab countries rejected at the time.
Also taking part in the meeting were Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, the presidents of the General Assembly and the Security Council and representatives of other bodies and U.N. delegations.
Arafat said this year's commemoration came at a time of "difficult circumstances, major challenges and enormous problems" for the Palestinian people.

He said the Palestinians maintained their commitment to a peace process that was "encountering major obstacles and is beset by enormous dangers because of the ongoing Israeli government policy of intransigence, procrastination and circumvention, of playing for time, of non-compliance with the deadlines established by the agreements already concluded."

He accused the Israeli government of "deliberately delaying the implementation of those provisions of the interim agreement that are still pending, primarily those concerning the redeployment of Israeli forces in Hebron," the last major West Bank town from which Israeli troops were to have largely withdrawn earlier this year.

Referring to the right-wing Israeli government, which replaced a Labour-led govenment after elections in May, he said it was conducting in Jerusalem "a wide-ranging campaign of systematic Judaization and settlement" and was maintaining "the closures and an economic embargo of our people on flimsy security-related grounds."
He was referring to the barring of large numbers of Palestinians from jobs in Israel after a series of suicide bombings last February and March.

Arafat said the world community was urged to induce Israel to comply with agreements already signed so that the peace process might continue and the Palestinian people "may complete the process of ending the Israeli occupation of its territory and its Holy Places and may regain and exercise its inalienable national rights, including the rights to return, to exercise self-determination and to establish an independent state with its capital at Jerusalem."
